questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A side length changes from 5 cm to 20 cm. What is the scale factor?

feedback.text: Correct. The scale factor is 20 divided by 5, which equals 4.
This subtracts the side lengths. Similarity uses a multiplier, not a difference.
This adds the side lengths. A scale factor compares matching sides by division.
This multiplies the two side lengths. Use new length divided by original length.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A 6-inch side is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. What is the new side length?

feedback.text: This adds 3 instead of multiplying. A scale factor is a multiplier.
This doubles instead of multiplying by 3.
Correct. 6 x 3 = 18 inches.
This uses the scale factor as the answer instead of applying it.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

Which value represents a reduction?

feedback.text: A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges the figure.
Correct. A scale factor between 0 and 1 reduces the figure.
A scale factor of 2 enlarges the figure.
A scale factor of 10 enlarges the figure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

On a scale drawing, 2 inches represents 14 feet. How many feet does 5 inches represent?

feedback.text: This adds 7 only once. Each inch represents 7 feet.
This represents 4 inches, not 5 inches.
This multiplies by 14 without first finding the feet per inch.
Correct. 2 inches represents 14 feet, so 1 inch represents 7 feet and 5 inches represents 35 feet.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

Which phrase best describes corresponding sides?

feedback.text: Corresponding sides are matching sides by position, not only the longest sides.

answer.text: Sides that match in the same position

feedback.text: Correct. Corresponding sides are compared to find scale factor.

answer.text: Any two sides in one figure

feedback.text: Sides must come from matching positions in similar figures.
Corresponding sides may not be equal; they are proportional.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A scale factor of 2.5 is applied to an 8-foot side. What is the new side length?

feedback.text: Correct. 8 x 2.5 = 20 feet.
This adds 2.5 instead of multiplying by the scale factor.
This uses a scale factor of 2 instead of 2.5.
This subtracts 2.5, but a scale factor is a multiplier.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

Two similar rectangles have matching sides 9 inches and 3 inches. If 9 inches is the new side and 3 inches is the original side, what is the scale factor?

feedback.text: This subtracts 3 from 9. Similarity uses division for scale factor.
This adds the side lengths. That does not give the multiplier.
This multiplies the side lengths. Scale factor compares them by division.
Correct. The scale factor is 9 divided by 3, which equals 3.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A 12-inch side is reduced by a scale factor of 1/3. What is the new side length?

feedback.text: This multiplies by 3 instead of by 1/3. The figure should get smaller.
This subtracts 3 instead of multiplying by 1/3.
Correct. 12 x (1/3) = 4 inches.
This leaves the side unchanged. A reduction changes the length.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

What stays the same in similar figures?

feedback.text: Correct. Similar figures keep the same shape while side lengths stay proportional.
Side lengths may change when a figure is enlarged or reduced.
Area usually changes when side lengths are scaled.
Perimeter can change when side lengths are scaled.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

On a map, 1 inch represents 20 miles. How many miles are represented by 6 inches?

feedback.text: This adds 20 and 6 instead of multiplying by the scale rate.
Correct. 6 x 20 = 120 miles.
This uses 10 miles per inch, not 20 miles per inch.
This divides instead of multiplying. More map inches represent more miles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A rectangle has a side of 4 cm. A similar rectangle has the matching side of 10 cm. A different side of the first rectangle is 6 cm. What is the matching side in the second rectangle?

feedback.text: This uses a scale factor of 2. The actual scale factor is 10 divided by 4.
This adds 2.5 only partway instead of multiplying 6 by the scale factor. Use the same multiplier for matching sides.
Correct. The scale factor is 10 divided by 4, then 6 x 2.5 = 15 cm.
This doubles 10 instead of applying the scale factor to the 6 cm side.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

Which action describes a dilation?

answer.text: Enlarging or reducing a figure by a scale factor

feedback.text: Correct. A dilation changes size using a scale factor while keeping shape.

answer.text: Sliding a figure without changing size

feedback.text: This describes a translation, not a dilation.

answer.text: Turning a figure around a point

feedback.text: This describes a rotation, not a dilation.

answer.text: Flipping a figure over a line

feedback.text: This describes a reflection, not a dilation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A scale model uses 1 inch for every 8 feet. How many feet are represented by 3 inches?

feedback.text: This adds 8 and 3. A scale relationship uses multiplication.
This represents 2 inches, not 3 inches.
This squares 8 or uses the wrong multiplier.
Correct. 3 x 8 = 24 feet.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

If a 10-inch side becomes a 5-inch side, what is the scale factor?

feedback.text: This compares original to new in the wrong direction for this question.
Correct. The scale factor is 5 divided by 10, which is 1/2.
This subtracts the side lengths. Similarity uses a ratio.
This adds the side lengths. Scale factor is not a sum.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A side length of 14 cm is enlarged by a scale factor of 2. What is the new length?

feedback.text: This adds 2 instead of multiplying by 2.
This divides by 2, which would reduce the length.
Correct. 14 x 2 = 28 cm.
This subtracts 2 instead of applying the scale factor.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

Which comparison should be used to find a scale factor from an original figure to a new figure?

feedback.text: Adding side lengths does not give the multiplier.
Subtracting gives a difference, not a scale factor.
Multiplying side lengths does not compare the change.

answer.text: new length divided by original length

feedback.text: Correct. This comparison gives the multiplier from original to new.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A scale factor greater than 1 produces what kind of change?

feedback.text: Correct. A scale factor greater than 1 makes each side length larger.
A reduction uses a scale factor between 0 and 1.
No change would use a scale factor of 1.
A reflection flips a figure and is not described by scale factor size change.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

On a blueprint, 4 inches represents 12 feet. How many feet does 1 inch represent?

feedback.text: This repeats the drawing measurement. Divide 12 feet by 4 inches.
Correct. 12 divided by 4 = 3 feet per inch.
This subtracts 4 from 12. Scale rate requires division.
This multiplies 4 and 12. Find the value for one inch instead.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A 30-inch side is reduced by a scale factor of 1/5. What is the new side length?

feedback.text: This multiplies by 5, which enlarges instead of reduces.
This subtracts 5 instead of multiplying by 1/5.
This leaves the side unchanged. A scale factor of 1/5 changes the length.
Correct. 30 x (1/5) = 6 inches.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_L02_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

Two figures are similar. One side in the first figure is 8 units, and the matching side in the second figure is 32 units. What is the scale factor from the first to the second?

feedback.text: This subtracts the side lengths. Similarity requires a multiplicative comparison.
This adds the side lengths. Scale factor is not a sum.
Correct. 32 divided by 8 = 4.
This multiplies the side lengths. Use division to compare matching sides.
